chunks: Suwayd al-Qallāʾ narrated from Ayyūb ibn Ḥurr, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who entrusted me with some wealth, then he died, and his children have nothing, and he had not performed the Hajj of Islam. He said: “Perform hajj on his behalf, and whatever remains, then give it to them.”

key_terms.اسْتَوْدَعَنِي: entrusted me with property as a deposit
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required in Islam
key_terms.مَالًا: wealth or property entrusted for safekeeping

ai.seo_question: What should be done with a deceased person’s trust deposit if he had not performed the obligatory hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a trust deposit left by a deceased person who had not yet performed the obligatory hajj. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that hajj be performed on behalf of the deceased from that wealth, and whatever remains should be given to his children.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2930 - Suwayd al-Qalla’ narrated from Ayyub ibn Harr, from Burayd al-‘Ijli, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked him about a man who entrusted me with some money, but he died without leaving anything for his children, and he had not performed the Hajj of Islam.
Imam (as) said: "Perform Hajj on his behalf, and whatever remains, give it to his children."
